Returns RpcInvalidParams when the type check fails, consistent 
with the existing pattern in this codebase.

title: Add TransactionProposalCancel for Cosign
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds the `TransactionProposalCancel` transaction (Cosigner Spec §7, transaction type 94): deletes a `TransactionProposal` ledger entry and releases the proposer's reserve. 

### Context of Change

Third transaction of the On-Chain Cosigner feature ([Cosigner spec](https://github.com/shawnxie999/XRPL-Standards/blob/cosign/XLS-0103-onchain-cosigner/README.md)), building on `TransactionProposalCreate` (#7887).

- While a proposal is live, only its Owner (the proposer) or its target (the proposed transaction's `Account`, or the `Delegate` named in it) may cancel: `tecNO_PERMISSION` otherwise.
- Once a proposal is terminal (its `Expiration` has passed, or the ledger sequence is strictly past the proposed transaction's `LastLedgerSequence`, mirroring the ordinary transactor's `tefMAX_LEDGER` rule), anyone may delete it.
- A zero `ProposalID` is `temMALFORMED`; a missing entry is `tecNO_ENTRY`.
- `isValidProposalTxnType` now also rejects proposing a Cancel, or any proposal transaction hidden inside a proposed Batch (XLS-0103 §5.3.1).
- Includes shared jtx helper `proposal::cancel` and a 19-case test suite covering authorization, terminal boundaries, Batch/multisign/sponsorship/ticket interactions, and nesting rejections.

### API Impact

- [x] `libxrpl` change (new amendment-gated transaction type, `featureCosign`)

title: fix: Enforce that MPT issuance flags are never cleared
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds a check to the `ValidMPTIssuance` invariant, gated on `fixCleanup3_5_0`: no transaction may clear a flag on an `MPTokenIssuance`. The one exception is `lsfMPTLocked`, which `tfMPTUnlock` clears legitimately.

### Context of Change

An external review of the lending code flagged `LoanPay` for moving a non-transferable MPT (the broker fee leg, borrower to broker owner) without a `lsfMPTCanTransfer` check. Triage showed the state is unreachable: the flag can be enabled after creation (`tfMPTSetCanTransfer` under DynamicMPT, set-once) but never cleared, and `VaultCreate` has refused a non-transferable asset since the first vault commit. No vault, and therefore no loan, can hold such an MPT.

That conclusion rests on one assumption: issuance flags never revert. Today only `MPTokenIssuanceSet::doApply` upholds it, by construction (flags are only ever ORed in). This PR enforces the assumption in one place, following the pattern already used for loan flags (`lsfLoanOverpayment`, `lsfLoanDefault`).

Earlier commits on this branch added a transferability gate to `LoanPay` fee routing. Since the state it guarded cannot exist, those changes are reverted in favor of the invariant.

### API Impact

- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)

## High Level Overview of Change

The `ValidConfidentialMPToken` invariant folded an erased MPToken's **pre-transaction** public balance into the confidential-state check, which is gated on the issuance's `sfConfidentialOutstandingAmount` (COA). Any transaction that drains an MPToken and erases it within the same `doApply` therefore failed with `tecINVARIANT_FAILED` as soon as *any unrelated holder* of the same issuance held a confidential balance.

This splits the public-balance rule out of the COA gate, gated on `fixCleanup3_5_0`.

## Context of Change

    changes_[id].deletedWithEncrypted = true;

title: fix: Resolve IntrusivePointer leak
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Fixes a leak and a missed partial destruction when `SharedWeakUnion::convertToWeak()` converts the last strong reference to a weak one. The old code also tripped a UBSan unsigned-underflow report in `IntrusiveRefCounts::releaseWeakRef()`.

## Context of Change

- `addWeakReleaseStrongRef()` returned `NoOp` when converting the only strong ref. The weak ref it adds keeps the weak count above zero, so this must be `PartialDestroy`. Because of this, `partialDestructor()` never ran and the partial-destroy-started bit was never set.
- `releaseWeakRef()` then took a fallback branch that was never meant to be reached. That branch subtracted `kWeakDelta` twice (the UBSan report) and passed the wrong expected values to `wait()`.
- `convertToWeak()` stored the pointer that `partialDestructorFinished()` had just set to null. The union lost the object and its weak ref was never released, so the object leaked. This bug already existed; the first fix makes it the common path, so both fixes must land together.

Affects `TreeNodeCache` (SHAMap nodes) through `TaggedCache::del()` and a race in `sweep()`. No change to transaction processing, so no amendment is needed.

Adds `IntrusiveSharedTest.convert_last_strong_to_weak` and `IntrusiveSharedTest.multithreaded_convert_to_weak_partial_delete`.

body:
Part 10/11 of a stack. Base: part 9 (`bthomee/shamap-stack-09-visit-differences-tests`).

## High Level Overview of Change

`NodePathStack` stored a `SHAMapNodeID` beside every node, so a traversal path carried two answers to
"where does this node sit" that could disagree. The path already answers it, so the stored ID is
removed and each node's depth is derived from the path's own length.

## Context of Change

A refactor. It responds to review feedback on #7942, which asked whether the stored ID could go away
entirely.

A SHAMap is a trie with a fan-out of 16 that does not maintain the radix merge property: adding an
item creates an inner node at every nibble the two keys share and never merges one away, so every
nibble down to a leaf has an inner node of its own and entry `i` of a path sits at depth `i`. That is
what makes the path's own length a complete answer, and the class docstring now says so, along with
the correction that this makes a SHAMap a trie rather than a radix tree.

`NodePathStack` therefore holds `std::vector<SHAMapTreeNodePtr>` and offers `topDepth()`. No consumer
wanted an ID: each wanted a depth and read the nibbles it cared about from a key it already held, so
`selectBranch` gains a depth overload and the ID-taking one becomes a thin wrapper for the sync paths
that hold real IDs. `unshareNode` takes a depth, since it only ever asked `isRoot()`.

What a path cannot derive is whether the caller descended the branches it says it did, so that much is
still recorded: one `uint256` of nibbles for the whole path rather than an ID per entry, and a leaf is
still judged against every branch recorded above it. Judging only the last nibble would accept a whole
subtree placed under the wrong branch, since one wrong child pointer leaves every leaf below it

title: fix: run passesLocalChecks on TransactionProposalCreate payload
body:
Per On-Chain Cosigner spec XLS-0103 §5.3.1 rule 2, a stored proposal must pass "the same [stateless format] checks it would receive if submitted directly", modulo the missing-signature exceptions the spec carves out.

TransactionProposalCreate::preflight was running xrpl::preflight (the transactor's own preflight chain) on the inner payload but not passesLocalChecks, even though checkValidity runs both on a direct submission. A payload that xrpl::preflight accepts but that fails isMemoOkay / isAccountFieldOkay / invalidMPTAmountInTx / isBatchRawTransactionOkay would therefore be stored on-ledger only to be rejected as temMALFORMED at completion time — the exact statically-dead proposal the spec forbids, squatting on the target's Ticket and owner reserve until Expiration.

Add the passesLocalChecks call alongside the existing xrpl::preflight call and cover it with a regression test that stores an oversized Memos payload (no transactor preflight step bounds memo size, so this test genuinely exercises the added check).
